reference_eligibility.title: Versioned metadata admission

facets.text: 0.5 is stored as Zarr v3 with OME metadata under attributes.ome (namespace), unlike the Zarr v2 .zattrs legacy layout
ome.version is a string. It MUST be consistent within a hierarchy, and legacy versions carry version inside multiscales
Admission requires explicit compatibility validation or a truthful unsupported result. There is no implicit legacy reinterpretation and no silent mixing of versions
evidence: 55 (AGAVE assumes zarr.json => 0.5; 'anything outside this assumption will error out in some way')
280-287 (reference reader defaults a missing multiscales version to '0.1')

facets.text: Distinguishing validation: a legacy layout next to an equivalent-looking 0.5 container, plus a hierarchy whose declared versions are inconsistent

reference_eligibility.reference_adjudication: consistent with the snapshot; no correction needed

facets.text: axes length equals array rank, and axes order equals array dimension order
Axis names are unique, and dimension_names in each level's zarr.json MUST match the axes names
There are 2 to 5 dimensions, with optional time and channel axes and arbitrary names. Semantics come from type, not from name or position
Navigation and slicing are tied to validated axis identity. An absent dimension is not the same as a length-one dimension, so no sliders or coordinates are invented
evidence: 222-223 (napari assumes 5D t,c,z,y,x when axes are missing)

facets.text: Rank or dimension_names mismatches are rejected rather than guessed
datasets[].path is group-relative with arbitrary names, and the declared list order (highest resolution first) is authoritative
Each level has its own coordinateTransformations, so geometry is level-specific
No folder or numeric ordering is assumed, and no fixed factor of 2. Non-2 and anisotropic or Z-downsampled pyramids exist and break peers
A declared level that is missing is handled explicitly
The selection UI and performance policy are a product choice
Dataset-level transforms are applied in order, and translation MUST follow scale
Multiscales (group-level) transforms are applied after the dataset-level ones
Units are SHOULD metadata. When a unit is absent, calibration is shown as unknown and never invented
A concrete composed check would expose reversed composition or omitted offsets (the reference probe gives (196,465))
evidence: 318-471 (viewers fail on translation and multiscale-level transforms)
266-283 (napari main keeps only ds_transforms[0] and the first group-level transform)

reference_eligibility.title: Associated label discovery and registration

facets.text: Label images are discovered through the parent image's labels group 'labels' path list. Intermediate groups are allowed
A label image implements multiscales with the same number of levels as the source image
Source association comes from image-label.source.image as a relative path (default ../../)
The level and coordinate relationship is resolved before overlaying. Labels are never attached by basename or equal shape, and unsupported geometry stays explicit
evidence: 2770 (equal level count does not imply the same downscaling or origin)

reference_eligibility.reference_adjudication: consistent. S035 L2770 reinforces facet C05.d

facets.text: Label pixels are integer dtypes, including uint64 and int64
colors and properties entries are keyed by label-value, not by list position
Categorical identity is preserved through lookup and resampling: nearest-neighbour sampling, no interpolated new IDs
Precision: exact 64-bit integers, or a declared supported range with refusal
facets.eligible: partial: dtype allowance is in the corpus, but binary64 or JS-number precision loss is derived rather than stated by any admitted source

facets.text: Palette is a reader SHOULD, not a format mandate

reference_eligibility.title: Metadata-driven chunk decoding

facets.text: Decode the codec chain each array declares (including sharding_indexed with inner codecs and index codecs such as crc32c)
Decoding runs the chain in reverse order
facets.limitation: The normative Zarr v3 core decoding-procedure text is absent from the admitted corpus (no zarr-specs capture in case/catalog.json)

facets.text: The bytes codec carries endianness, so little-endian cannot be assumed
The transpose codec changes the encoded layout
evidence: 553,600 (tensorstore transpose+sharding bug and semantics, issue text only)
facets.eligible: partial: issue text only, no normative spec

facets.text: There is an explicit support boundary, and unsupported codec or dtype combinations are refused rather than displayed as pixels

reference_eligibility.reference_adjudication: not mistaken; decisive normative Zarr v3 codec text is unavailable in this corpus, so C07.b is unassessable_missing_input at facet level

reference_eligibility.title: Absent data versus failed reads

facets.text: fill_value defines uninitialized or absent chunks, so an absent chunk is valid fill data
facets.limitation: Normative fill_value and store-interface semantics (zarr-specs core and stores) are absent from the admitted corpus

facets.text: Read, decode or cancellation failures are distinguished from absent or fill data, and failures are never zero-filled
evidence: 3840,3887 (a parse_url store reads arrays as all zeros)
223-231 (parse_url collapses error and absence to None)

facets.text: Readable and writable are distinct capabilities. Reader-side writes must be prevented, and source data is never repaired
The actual state is shown

novel_findings.text: HCS plates need an explicit product decision: full navigation or detect-and-list. Peers crash or degrade on plates, and canonical 0.5 plates exist as fixtures.

novel_findings.text: A chooser for multiple multiscales entries is an optional or deferred capability, since no peer opens beyond the first entry.
novel_findings.note: Thinner than X2's version: no spec choose-by-name rule

novel_findings.text: omero metadata is optional. The reference reader degrades gracefully when it is partial, so channel controls need defaults.
Honouring rdefs.defaultT/defaultZ is an optional differentiator. WEBKNOSSOS ignores them, and a real sample has defaultZ 118.
novel_findings.plan_applicability: Plan L5 time-point and plane selection (optional)

novel_findings.text: Groups that hold only a single array (no multiscales) need a defined behaviour: render with default scale or give an explicit message. ngff#207 is open and ome-zarr-py renders raw arrays.
novel_findings.plan_applicability: Plan L7 and L11 feedback for unsupported input

novel_findings.text: In 0.5 a label image cannot be told apart from an image except through the parent labels list, so the image list must not present label images as standalone images.
novel_findings.plan_applicability: Plan L5 'lists the images it finds'

novel_findings.text: Opening at a labels/ subfolder or a label-image group should navigate to the parent image. An unknown root should give a defined message rather than a silent no-op.
novel_findings.plan_applicability: Plan L5 discovery and L7 feedback

novel_findings.text: Pair malformed fixtures with ome-ngff-validator runs, using its schemas query parameter.

correct_non_findings.text: Zipped OME-Zarr (.ozx, RFC-9) and zip stores are deferred because RFC-9 is unreleased. The citation is corrected to S035 L4500 and S052 #619.
The '12-viewer' matrix is actually 11 viewers, and the substantive claim (no viewer opens beyond the first multiscales entry) stands.
'9846318 (÷3 factors)' is unverified: S043 says only 'not equal to 2'.
Optional capabilities (rdefs defaults, memory-estimate picker, time-unit display, multi-multiscales chooser, resource lifecycle) are correctly not presented as requirements.

AGAVE desktop-analog prior art supports the Plan's existing background-read and cancel obligation (covered): the blocking-load issue is still open (S103), and session-local settings contrast with AGAVE's absolute-path settings JSON (S108 L27).
Real 0.5 filesets (S054, S055, S056) carry no group-level transforms, and the frequency question is kept open rather than dismissed.

novel_findings.text: Multiple multiscales entries: the spec lets the user choose by name with the first entry as fallback, while the ecosystem opens only the first entry and some viewers crash. omero is optional, so fallback defaults are a required path: bioformats2raw --no-minmax, ome-zarr-py degrades gracefully, and vizarr fails to load labels when omero is missing (counterexample).

comparison_X1_vs_X2.verdict: Neither result retains any reference, and both lose most of what their own upstream stages had acquired. X1 keeps more reference facets (C05 and C06 survive, C04 composition order survives) and more distinct novel findings. X2 keeps C02 and more usable C03, C07 and C08 facets, and its corrections are more accurate on the whole. Each has exactly one false 'unsupported' dismissal of a correct S034 figure. X2's error is more consequential (it removes the TB-scale anchor), while X1 has more low-severity false or overstated claims (five vs four, one of them negligible). By finding identity this is not a dominance relation: each has facets the other lacks, and no net score is computed (SCORING).

neither_result.text: The reference reader defaults a missing multiscales version to '0.1', so 0.5 axes are parsed under 0.1 format rules: an implicit legacy reinterpretation in ome-zarr-py.
dimension_names MUST match axes (a 0.5.2 clarification), and napari assumes 5D when axes are absent.
napari-ome-zarr main keeps only datasets[0].coordinateTransformations[0] and only the first group-level transform, so dataset-level and group-level translations are dropped.
Equal label and image level counts do not guarantee the same downscaling or origin (ngff issue).
Label values are keyed by label-value, and nearest-neighbour resampling is needed for categorical data.
A parse_url store silently reads arrays as all zeros, and the reference reader zero-fills tiles on load ValueError.
